theme: The Battle for Zendikar: Rise of the Gatewatch, Fall of the Titans
status: FINISHED STORY-FIRST PROPOSAL — awaiting Cory's approval; one explicitly authorized banned card
narrator_note: Tazri commanded survivors, defended Sea Gate, and oversaw restoration. Her later five-color identity unites Kor, Merfolk, Vampire, Elf, Goblin, Planeswalker, and Eldrazi portraits in the story. She is chosen for history, not power.
canon_caveats: Emrakul, the Aeons Torn is banned in ordinary Commander and is included only by Cory's explicitly requested story-first house-rule exception. Mark deck as unsanctioned; do not report zero legality problems.
There were three true Eldrazi titans. Brood creatures are extensions of those titans, not separate plane-devouring entities.
Ulamog and Kozilek were destroyed by the four founding Gatewatch members. Emrakul departed to Innistrad and was NOT destroyed on Zendikar.
Ugin, Sorin and Nahiri were the ancient jailers. Nahiri subsequently stood vigil alone, but her later history and Emrakul's Innistrad story are separate arcs.
Bolas manipulated Jace, Chandra and Sarkhan to reactivate the Eye, releasing broods first, while the titans were initially still bound.
The brief Aligned Hedron Network entrapment of Ulamog failed due to Ob Nixilis's interference and Kozilek's arrival. It was not the final destruction of the titans.
Kiora joined the war with Thassa's stolen bident but was not one of the four founding Oath-taking Gatewatch members.
Tazri, Beacon of Unity, Drana, the Last Bloodchief and Sea Gate Restoration are historical aftermath cards printed later in Zendikar Rising.
Bident of Thassa is originally a Theros card but physically traveled with Kiora to Zendikar and is a deliberate cross-plane artifact.
Traditional Commander legality is waived for Emrakul only; all other checks are still performed.

beats.title: I. The ancient prison and its first unraveling

cards.name: Nahiri, the Lithomancer
cards.why: Nahiri constructed Zendikar's worldwide hedron prison to contain the three Eldrazi titans.

cards.name: Sorin Markov
cards.why: The vampire planeswalker helped Nahiri and Ugin set the ancient trap.

cards.name: Ugin, the Spirit Dragon
cards.why: Ugin designed the strategy behind the titans' imprisonment, even though this printing's art is from Tarkir.

cards.name: Hedron Matrix
cards.why: The original ROE flavor recalls the prison's massive stone network awakening as the Eldrazi stirred.

cards.name: Eldrazi Monument
cards.why: Zendikari traces of the three titans as myths and divine idols; an original ZEN artifact, not proof of literal worship at this exact location.

cards.name: Quest for Ula's Temple
cards.why: Ula was Zendikar's mythic interpretation of Ulamog; this WWK card records that pre-release religion.

cards.name: Cosi's Trickster
cards.why: Cosi was the trickster of Zendikar's merfolk myth, connected to their ancient, misremembered Eldrazi.

cards.name: Nicol Bolas, Planeswalker
cards.why: Bolas engineered the convergence of Sarkhan, Jace and Chandra at the Eye of Ugin for his own ends.

cards.name: Sarkhan Vol
cards.why: The dragon-obsessed Planeswalker was Bolas's operative at the fateful Eye of Ugin incident.

cards.name: Jace, the Mind Sculptor
cards.why: A period portrait of Jace, whose encounter at the Eye unwittingly helps unleash the broods.

cards.name: Chandra Ablaze
cards.why: A period portrait of Chandra, whose magic helped reactivate the Eye when Bolas's trap unfolded.

cards.name: Nissa Revane
cards.why: Zendikar's native planeswalker intervenes as the old hedron prison destabilizes, with grave consequences.

cards.name: Emrakul, the Aeons Torn
cards.why: The ORIGINAL third Titan. She is later absent from the final Sea Gate battle; intentionally included even though Commander-banned.

cards.name: Ulamog, the Infinite Gyre
cards.why: The original physical depiction of Ulamog before his later cease-less-hunger portrayal.

cards.name: Kozilek, Butcher of Truth
cards.why: The original Kozilek depiction, corresponding to Zendikar's misremembered trickster god Cosi.

beats.title: II. The Eldrazi awaken and consume Zendikar

cards.name: Awakening Zone
cards.why: ROE-era Eldrazi spawning grounds represent the transition from captivity to invasion.

cards.name: Skittering Invasion
cards.why: The old expansion's devastating swarm of Eldrazi spawn overruns Zendikar.

cards.name: Eldrazi Conscription
cards.why: The loss of individuality as the titan's influence consumes other creatures.

cards.name: Hand of Emrakul
cards.why: One of Emrakul's original brood manifestations before she departs Zendikar.

cards.name: Emrakul's Hatcher
cards.why: Emrakul's lesser spawn during the initial awakening, not evidence she was present for the final battle.

cards.name: Pathrazer of Ulamog
cards.why: A Ulamog brood creature breaking the landscape in the original invasion era.

cards.name: Artisan of Kozilek
cards.why: The Kozilek lineage's eldritch alteration of the plane.

cards.name: It That Betrays
cards.why: A terrifying original-era Eldrazi manifestation of the attack on mortals.

cards.name: Ulamog, the Ceaseless Hunger
cards.why: Ulamog's actual BFZ printing as the foremost titan ravaging the plane in the 2015 conflict.

cards.name: Desolation Twin
cards.why: A direct BFZ-era vision of the titan broods and their destructive scale.

cards.name: Breaker of Armies
cards.why: The enormous Ulamog-aligned monstrosity confronting the Zendikari defenders.

cards.name: Ulamog's Nullifier
cards.why: A named agent of Ulamog's army, part of the assault on Zendikar.

cards.name: Void Winnower
cards.why: BFZ-era Eldrazi that makes the catastrophic distortion of reality visible.

cards.name: Gideon's Reproach
cards.why: An early defender's response to the monstrous invaders in the original set.

beats.title: III. Sea Gate's coalition and the temporary hedron victory

cards.name: Gideon, Ally of Zendikar
cards.why: Gideon rallies survivors after the catastrophic fall of Sea Gate.

cards.name: Ugin's Insight
cards.why: The original quote warns Jace that THREE titans came to Zendikar; critical to the prison strategy.

cards.name: Nissa, Voice of Zendikar
cards.why: Nissa's later portrait as she connects to the plane's soul and leylines.

cards.name: Kiora, Master of the Depths
cards.why: Kiora returns with stolen sea-god power and a summoned aquatic army.

cards.name: Chandra, Flamecaller
cards.why: The fire mage arrives and helps the other Planeswalkers defend Zendikar.

cards.name: General Tazri
cards.why: The original wartime Tazri, leading Gideon's forces and survivors when their commander is absent.

cards.name: Munda, Ambush Leader
cards.why: A prominent Zendikari Ally commander resisting the Eldrazi.

cards.name: Drana, Liberator of Malakir
cards.why: The vampire queen changes sides and joins the anti-Eldrazi coalition.

cards.name: Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet
cards.why: The rival vampire lord represents those who exploited the crisis rather than joining the coalition.

cards.name: Noyan Dar, Roil Shaper
cards.why: His roilmages help defend Sea Gate and turn Zendikar's living land against the broods.

cards.name: Jori En, Ruin Diver
cards.why: The merfolk scholar assists Jace and later brings news of Ulamog's approach.

cards.name: Zada, Hedron Grinder
cards.why: A goblin Ally directly named for Zendikar's original hedron technology.

cards.name: Omnath, Locus of Rage
cards.why: The elemental manifestation of Zendikar's fury, a world-soul theme rather than a documented single battle speech.

cards.name: Unified Front
cards.why: Original BFZ flavor documents the disparate defenders standing together.

cards.name: Allied Reinforcements
cards.why: The OGW original quote honors the collective defense.

cards.name: Roil's Retribution
cards.why: Original text depicts survivors using the Eldrazi's hunger against them.

cards.name: Nissa's Renewal
cards.why: Direct BFZ event: Nissa regains her connection to Zendikar's heart.

cards.name: Aligned Hedron Network
cards.why: The originally printed scene shows Ulamog briefly trapped in a restored hedron array.

beats.title: IV. Ob Nixilis shatters the trap; Kozilek returns and the Gatewatch forms

cards.name: Ob Nixilis, the Fallen
cards.why: The old Zendikar printing shows the demon before he regains his Planeswalker spark.

cards.name: Ob Nixilis Reignited
cards.why: Ob Nixilis uses the hedron array's power to regain his spark and frees Ulamog.

cards.name: Hedron Alignment
cards.why: The spell/geometry of maintaining an Eldrazi prison; a thematic supplement to Aligned Hedron Network, not a second proven imprisonment.

cards.name: Kozilek, the Great Distortion
cards.why: Kozilek's actual OGW-era form as he rises beneath Zendikar's surface.

cards.name: Kozilek's Return
cards.why: The named return of the second titan makes the land itself warp.

cards.name: World Breaker
cards.why: The OGW Eldrazi devastating and reshaping the world under Kozilek's emergence.

cards.name: Oath of Gideon
cards.why: The Gideon oath helps formally found the original Gatewatch.

cards.name: Oath of Jace
cards.why: Jace resolves to stay and help protect other planes, despite the ability to flee.

cards.name: Oath of Chandra
cards.why: Chandra's promise to join the fight as a founding Gatewatch member.

cards.name: Oath of Nissa
cards.why: Nissa takes the fourth original Gatewatch oath.

cards.name: Call the Gatewatch
cards.why: Original Jace quotation explains why planeswalkers choose to stay in danger.

cards.name: Roiling Waters
cards.why: Noyan Dar's roilmages command Zendikar's unstable waters against the enemy.

beats.title: V. The Last Stand: two titans fall, one escapes, Zendikar endures

cards.name: Witness the End
cards.why: The original OGW quote records the despair when Kozilek emerged just as Ulamog was trapped.

cards.name: Bident of Thassa
cards.why: Kiora's stolen THEROS god-weapon, which she actually wields against the Eldrazi on Zendikar.

cards.name: Planar Outburst
cards.why: The plane's convulsions during the final Eldrazi conflict; a contextual BFZ rather than a precise named finale scene.

cards.name: Nissa's Judgment
cards.why: Nissa and Zendikar's earth/elemental energy power the final counterattack.

cards.name: Fall of the Titans
cards.why: Original OGW flavor explicitly records Gideon containing the broods while Chandra burns the bound Ulamog and Kozilek.

cards.name: Ruin in Their Wake
cards.why: The world devastated by the titans, a contemporary portrait of what the survivors must rebuild.

cards.name: Natural State
cards.why: Original OGW flavor captures the determination to erase the Eldrazi's damage.

cards.name: Zendikar Resurgent
cards.why: Named card of Zendikar's recovery following the destruction of the two titans.

cards.name: Drana, the Last Bloodchief
cards.why: A later portrait of the surviving vampire leader in the recovering Zendikar.

cards.name: Sea Gate Restoration
cards.why: A later double-faced card and original Tazri flavor remembering the defenders while rebuilding Sea Gate.

beats.title: VI. The battlefield map: Eye, hedrons, ruins and restoration — lands

cards.name: Eye of Ugin
cards.why: Location of the ancient prison's focal point and Bolas's manipulated accidental opening.

cards.name: Sanctum of Ugin
cards.why: An Ugin-associated refuge/hedronic locus related to understanding the Eldrazi.

cards.name: Eldrazi Temple
cards.why: Old Zendikar temple representing reverence and eldritch sites.

cards.name: Shrine of the Forsaken Gods
cards.why: Original BFZ land and flavor link the Eldrazi titans to Zendikar's former religious cults.

cards.name: Sea Gate Wreckage
cards.why: The OGW land's flavor remembers the city's destruction and lost knowledge.

cards.name: Ally Encampment
cards.why: A camp housing Zendikar's multi-race resistance.

cards.name: Holdout Settlement
cards.why: An OGW wartime survivor settlement; physical evidence of civilian endurance.

cards.name: Corrupted Crossroads
cards.why: Land transformed by the corrupted titan presence and unstable magic.

cards.name: Mirrorpool
cards.why: Landscape shaped by Kozilek-like temporal/reflection distortions; contextual, not a named event.

cards.name: Ruins of Oran-Rief
cards.why: Aftermath of the destruction of one of Zendikar's lush regions.

cards.name: Blighted Cataract
cards.why: Blue regional land illustrating the Eldrazi blight's geographical reach.

cards.name: Blighted Fen
cards.why: Black regional land illustrating the Eldrazi blight's geographical reach.

cards.name: Blighted Gorge
cards.why: Red regional land illustrating the Eldrazi blight's geographical reach.

cards.name: Blighted Steppe
cards.why: White regional land illustrating the Eldrazi blight's geographical reach.

cards.name: Blighted Woodland
cards.why: Green regional land illustrating the Eldrazi blight's geographical reach.

cards.name: Emeria, the Sky Ruin
cards.why: The ancient false divine identity of Emrakul survives in Zendikari religious geography.

cards.name: Valakut, the Molten Pinnacle
cards.why: Original volcanic Zendikar terrain, a backdrop to the plane's violent Roil.

cards.name: Oran-Rief, the Vastwood
cards.why: Nissa and the elves' original lush homeland later devastated by the Eldrazi.

cards.name: Bojuka Bog
cards.why: The black-mana landscape associated with the vampires and death-haunted parts of Zendikar.

cards.name: Crumbling Vestige
cards.why: OGW land showing the world breaking under Eldrazi assault.
